company.text: New Belgium was founded in **1991** in Fort Collins, Colorado, by Kim Jordan and Jeff Lebesch. It was sold to **Lion**, Kirin's Australian beverage arm, in **2019**. Lion then bought **Bell's Brewery** (Michigan) in **2021** and put it under New Belgium. Breweries: **Fort Collins**, **Asheville NC** (hit by Hurricane Helene in 2024, now back online), and **Daleville VA** (bought from Constellation in 2023). Brands: **Voodoo Ranger** (the US's top craft IPA family; Imperial IPA was No. 1 craft beer in c-stores per Circana), **Fat Tire** (recipe changed in 2023), Bell's Two Hearted, plus beyond-beer: Voodoo Ranger Hardcharged Tea, LightStrike refreshers and RTDs. CEO is **Shaun Belongie** (former CMO, CEO since Nov 2023). His strategy is "radical simplicity": focus on three big brands. Since 2025 New Belgium also brews Kirin beer for the US. Hospitality: taprooms in Fort Collins, Asheville and Denver; the San Francisco brewpub **closed in Feb 2024**; a Mohegan Sun (CT) taproom was announced (**status to be confirmed**).

financials.country: US, private (subsidiary of Lion / Kirin Holdings, listed in Tokyo)
financials.text: New Belgium does not publish its own numbers. **Estimates:** revenue **~$219M** and **~609 employees** (RocketReach, 2026); this looks low for a 1M+ barrel brewer, so treat as a floor (**to be confirmed**). Older data: **$245M revenue (2015)**, **~958,000 barrels (2016)**, **703 employees (2018)**. In 2021, New Belgium and Bell's together had about **$361M** in tracked off-premise sales year-to-date (Brewbound). The Voodoo Ranger family alone passed **1M barrels** a year (brand estimate, Nov 2025). Kirin Holdings reports Lion results but not a New Belgium line.

This matches the campaign pattern: warm leads stall at the work-email step.

industry.title: Display space is the battleground
industry.text: Beer volumes are soft, so brewers fight for **display space** in grocery and c-stores (Bump Williams Consulting via Brewbound, 2025). Better POS execution protects that space.

industry.title: Convenience is the growth channel
industry.text: C-stores are craft's No. 1 growth channel. Voodoo Ranger built its lead there and held close to **15% of craft c-store dollars** (Circana, 2023). C-store POS is high volume, small format and hard to verify in-store.

industry.title: Beyond beer means new shelves
industry.text: Hardcharged Tea, RTDs and refreshers sit on **different shelves** (hard tea, RTD), so each needs its own POS and planogram. New Belgium itself said placement drives Hardcharged's success.

industry.title: Taprooms under pressure
industry.text: Big brewers are closing taprooms (New Belgium SF, 2024; AB InBev too). The ones that stay must work harder as **brand experiences**.

talking_points: How do you manage POS for Voodoo Ranger across c-stores and grocery today: one agency, many printers, or your distributors?
Do you know how much of your in-store material actually gets installed?
With Hardcharged and the RTDs on different shelves, how many separate POS kits do you run per season?
How do the taprooms tie into retail marketing: shared creative, or separate programs?
Who else signs off on in-store spend: procurement, brand, or distributors?
What does a good 2027 look like for your team, and what would you change first?

attention.title: US, not Canada
attention.text: The campaign now focuses on **Canada**. New Belgium is US-only (Canada distribution **to be confirmed**). Keep it, the title is strong, but flag it to the team.

attention.title: Distributors pay for some POS
attention.text: In US beer, distributors often place and fund POS. Ask who controls the budget before pitching savings.

attention.title: Cost pressure
attention.text: New Belgium has had several small layoffs and restructurings (Bell's merger in 2022; sales and marketing restructure). Pitch savings and simplicity, not big creative spend.
